Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

battle noun

also battles, combat, battlefield, fight a battle

classical

Liv. 21.4.8
Cic. Div. 1.77: proelium committere (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 185

proelium, proeliī n.

noun, second declension

battle, combat

To join battle, proelium committere; to fight a battle, proelium facere (Traupman 185); in battle, proeliō.

Examples

  • prīnceps in proelium ībat, ultimus cōnsertō proeliō excēdēbat

    he was the first to go into battle and the last to leave it once it was joinedLiv. 21.4.8

  • pugnā … magnā victī sumus

    we have been beaten in a great battleLiv. 22.7.8

Other words

  • pugna, pugnae f. — a fight, a battle

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Liv. 22.7.8; Traupman 185

    Properly a fight man to man (Lewis & Short); also a single combat.

  • aciēs, aciēī f. — the battle line; a pitched battle

    noun, fifth declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.22: aciem īnstruere (Lewis & Short); Traupman 185

    The front of an army drawn up for battle, its ‘edge’ (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s battlefield.

See also war, army, soldier, victory, defeat, enemy.
